questions.stem: In a Lakeflow job, how does one task wait for another?

options.text: It polls the other task's output table in a loop
Tasks always run in the order they were created
It lists the other task in its Depends on setting
It must be placed in a separate job

questions.explanation: Depends on sets a task's upstream tasks; by default it runs when they have all succeeded.

questions.stem: A notebook task computes a file count that a later task needs. What is the supported way to pass it?

options.text: Write it to a global Python variable
Set a task value in the first task and read it in the later task
Store it in the cluster's environment variables
Print it and parse the job log

questions.explanation: Task values let a task set a small value that downstream tasks in the same run can read.

questions.stem: Which of these are task types a Lakeflow job can run? Choose three.
questions.explanation: Jobs run notebooks, SQL, pipelines and more; there is no email inbox task type.

questions.stem: Arrange the tasks of a medallion job in a valid dependency order.
questions.explanation: Each layer depends on the one before it, so the tasks form a chain from bronze to the dashboard.

questions.stem: What do the tasks in a Fernhill job and their dependencies form?

options.text: A loop that repeats until a task fails

questions.explanation: A job's tasks and their dependencies form a directed acyclic graph.
